newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ireland's Bruton sees EU as political model.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Bruton sees EU as political model.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton made a passionate appeal to European Union members on Wednesday to prove to their citizens that the bloc was a political model for the future.
In a speech to the European Parliament, Bruton said Europe's people were not sufficiently engaged by what the bloc was doing.
"To win the hearts of Europeans, at this stage in its history, the European Union must show that it is the best vehicle through which the continent can prepare for the world of tommorrow," he said.
Bruton, whose country is current EU president, said the days when people had but one sovereign allegiance were fast coming to an end.
Instant communications and mobility in the 21st century would mean nationalites became more and more intertwined.
"In many parts of the world, a new political model is needed to organise this new social reality -- a model that recognises that people often have more allegiances than one," Bruton said.

The EU was such a model. "In the European Union someone can, at the same time, owe allegiance to Flanders, Belgium and to Europe, and yet share the same working and living space with someone who has a different set of allegiances," he said.
But Bruton also warned against expecting too much.
"We must not ask Europe, or the European Union, to perform the impossible and then judge it severely when it fails.
"In an age of multiple allegiances, the Union will never be more than just one of the entities to which Europe's citizens will feel allegiance," he said.

Turning to the inter-governmental conference (IGC), Bruton said the negotiations offered a unique opportunity for the Union to bring its work closer to the public, particularly if it endorsed the concept of transparency.
He called for the IGC to strengthen the role of the Parliament, a statement that not surprisingly triggered a round of applause from MEPs.
But dismissing the comments of many EU officials and some leaders, he said the IGC was making progress.
"We are moving from the aspirational to the concrete," he said.
